questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The officer said to the clerk, "Bring the file at once."
o: The officer requested the clerk to brought the file at once.
The officer ordered the clerk to bring the file at once.
The officer ordered the clerk that he brings the file at once.
The officer said to the clerk that bring the file at once.
questions.x: Commands use an introductory verb such as 'ordered' + object + to-infinitive.

questions.q: The company was declared ____ when it could no longer pay its creditors.
questions.x: Insolvent: unable to pay debts.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
The manager, as well as the clerks, (are) responsible for the error.
questions.x: Correct answer: is. With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject.

questions.q: I wish I ____ more time to prepare for yesterday's interview.
questions.x: Correct answer: had had. A wish about the past uses the past perfect.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: 'The pen is mightier than the sword.'
questions.x: Correct answer: Metonymy. 'Pen' and 'sword' stand for writing and military force.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: He would then read its clauses aloud to the workers.
Q: Every morning the supervisor opened the rulebook.
R: Over time, the workers began quoting the rules back to him.
S: He picked one rule for the day.
questions.x: Opening the book → picking a rule → reading it → the result over time.

questions.q: The patient has been suffering ____ fever for three days.
questions.x: 'Suffer from' is the standard collocation for an illness.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
She is / the most unique candidate / we have interviewed so far.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'the most unique candidate'. 'Unique' is absolute and cannot take 'most'.

questions.q: The speaker spoke so softly that we could ____ hear him.
questions.x: 'Hardly' means almost not.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The new policy seeks to mitigate the hardship faced by migrant workers', the word 'mitigate' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lessen. Mitigate: make less severe.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The costly new building turned out to be a white elephant', the idiom means:
o: A possession that costs much to maintain but is of little use
questions.x: Correct answer: A possession that costs much to maintain but is of little use. A white elephant is costly and burdensome.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The accused / was acquitted from / all the charges framed against him.
o: all the charges framed against him.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'was acquitted from'. One is 'acquitted of' a charge.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
The poor (is) often the worst affected by rising prices.
questions.x: Correct answer: are. 'The poor' means poor people and takes a plural verb.

questions.q: According to the passage, a strong foundation in the first language:
o: Can make learning a second language easier
Prevents children from learning other languages
questions.x: Answer: 'Can make learning a second language easier'. The passage cites research to this effect. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Children learn best when they first understand what they are being taught. A child who must learn arithmetic and science in a language she barely speaks spends her energy decoding words rather than grasping ideas. Teaching in the mother tongue in the early years does not shut the door to other languages; research suggests that a strong first language makes it easier to learn a second. The choice is not between the mother tongue and a global language, but about the order in which they are taught.

questions.q: What does the author mean by 'the order in which they are taught'?
o: The mother tongue should come first, followed by other languages
Only one language should ever be taught
Languages should be taught in alphabetical order
Global languages must be taught before the mother tongue
questions.x: Answer: 'The mother tongue should come first, followed by other languages'. The author favours the mother tongue in the early years. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Children learn best when they first understand what they are being taught. A child who must learn arithmetic and science in a language she barely speaks spends her energy decoding words rather than grasping ideas. Teaching in the mother tongue in the early years does not shut the door to other languages; research suggests that a strong first language makes it easier to learn a second. The choice is not between the mother tongue and a global language, but about the order in which they are taught.

questions.q: Which of the following would weaken the author's argument?
o: Evidence that decoding words takes mental effort
Evidence that children taught first in a second language learn concepts equally well
Evidence that bilingual children do well in later years
Evidence that children understand more in their mother tongue
questions.x: Answer: 'Evidence that children taught first in a second language learn concepts equally well'. That would contradict the claim that mother-tongue teaching aids understanding. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Children learn best when they first understand what they are being taught. A child who must learn arithmetic and science in a language she barely speaks spends her energy decoding words rather than grasping ideas. Teaching in the mother tongue in the early years does not shut the door to other languages; research suggests that a strong first language makes it easier to learn a second. The choice is not between the mother tongue and a global language, but about the order in which they are taught.

questions.q: According to the passage, why will adding judges alone not end delays?
o: There is no shortage of judges
Judges refuse to hear simple cases
Procedural problems such as frequent adjournments would remain
questions.x: Answer: 'Procedural problems such as frequent adjournments would remain'. Adjournments, summons and clogged queues are named. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Delay in courts is often blamed on a shortage of judges, and the shortage is real. But adding judges alone will not cure delay if cases are adjourned repeatedly, if summons are not served on time, and if simple disputes clog the same queue as complex ones. Mediation and specialised fast-track forums can divert matters that do not need a full trial. Justice delayed is not merely justice denied; it also teaches people that the law is not worth invoking.

questions.q: The last sentence suggests that judicial delay also:
o: Makes courts more efficient over time
Reduces people's faith in using the law
questions.x: Answer: 'Reduces people's faith in using the law'. It 'teaches people that the law is not worth invoking'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Delay in courts is often blamed on a shortage of judges, and the shortage is real. But adding judges alone will not cure delay if cases are adjourned repeatedly, if summons are not served on time, and if simple disputes clog the same queue as complex ones. Mediation and specialised fast-track forums can divert matters that do not need a full trial. Justice delayed is not merely justice denied; it also teaches people that the law is not worth invoking.

questions.q: The author proposes mediation and fast-track forums mainly to:
o: Divert matters that do not need a full trial
questions.x: Answer: 'Divert matters that do not need a full trial'. This is stated in the third sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Delay in courts is often blamed on a shortage of judges, and the shortage is real. But adding judges alone will not cure delay if cases are adjourned repeatedly, if summons are not served on time, and if simple disputes clog the same queue as complex ones. Mediation and specialised fast-track forums can divert matters that do not need a full trial. Justice delayed is not merely justice denied; it also teaches people that the law is not worth invoking.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Indigo Revolt (1859–60):
1. It took place in Bengal against European planters.
2. Dinabandhu Mitra's play 'Neel Darpan' depicted the planters' oppression.
3. It was crushed without any government inquiry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The government appointed the Indigo Commission (1860).

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Lahore Session (Purna Swaraj) 2. Nehru Report 3. Simon Commission's arrival 4. First Round Table Conference
questions.x: Simon Commission (Feb 1928), Nehru Report (Aug 1928), Lahore (Dec 1929), First RTC (Nov 1930).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Vijayanagara Empire:
1. It was founded by Harihara and Bukka in the 14th century.
2. Krishnadevaraya wrote 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu.
3. Its capital Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Charter Act of 1833:
1. It made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
2. It ended the East India Company's activities as a commercial body.
3. It introduced open competition for civil services, which was implemented immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Open competition was proposed later (Charter Act 1853) and the first exam was held in 1855.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the mansabdari system:
1. It was organised under Akbar.
2. 'Zat' fixed personal rank and salary, while 'sawar' indicated the number of horsemen to be maintained.
3. Mansabs were hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Mansabs were not hereditary; the emperor could transfer or withdraw them.

questions.q:
Which of the following are recognised as classical dances by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
1. Kathakali
2. Manipuri
3. Sattriya
4. Garba
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Garba is a folk dance.

questions.q:
Which of the following are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India?
1. Rani-ki-Vav, Patan
2. Hoysala temples (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura)
3. Santiniketan
4. Gateway of India
How many of the above are World Heritage Sites?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The Gateway of India is not a World Heritage Site.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Poona Pact (1932) is correct?
o: It increased reserved seats for depressed classes within joint electorates, replacing separate electorates under the Communal Award
It granted separate electorates to depressed classes
It was signed between Gandhi and Jinnah
It ended the Civil Disobedience Movement
questions.x: It was signed by Gandhi and Ambedkar after Gandhi's fast in Yerawada jail.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Aligarh movement:
1. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875.
2. It promoted modern, Western education among Muslims.
3. It launched the Khilafat movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Khilafat movement (1919–24) was led by the Ali brothers and others.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Mountbatten Plan advanced the date of transfer of power to August 1947.
Reason (R): Communal violence and administrative breakdown made a quick transfer seem necessary.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about ASEAN:
1. Timor-Leste became its eleventh member in October 2025.
2. Its secretariat is in Jakarta.
3. India is a full member of ASEAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India is a dialogue partner (Comprehensive Strategic Partnership).

questions.q:
The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 replaced which of the following?
1. The Foreigners Act, 1946
2. The Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939
3. The Citizenship Act, 1955
Which of the above were replaced?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It also replaced the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920 and the Immigration (Carriers' Liability) Act, 2000; the Citizenship Act continues.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Census:
1. The next Census will include enumeration of caste.
2. Its reference date is 1 March 2027 for most of the country.
3. It will be conducted entirely on paper schedules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is planned as the first digital census, using mobile applications.

questions.q:
With the Labour Codes coming into force in November 2025, which of the following became part of the law?
1. Fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after one year of continuous service.
2. Issue of appointment letters to all workers is mandatory.
3. Employers must provide a free annual health check-up to workers above 40 years of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three were among the headline changes publicised when the Codes were notified.

questions.q: Which scheme approved in July 2025 aims to improve agricultural productivity in 100 low-performing districts by converging existing schemes?
questions.x: Correct answer: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana. It is modelled on the Aspirational Districts approach.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 'Viksit Bharat @2047' vision:
1. It aims at India becoming a developed nation by the centenary of independence.
2. NITI Aayog has prepared documents and frameworks for it.
3. It is a constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is a policy vision.

questions.q:
Match the 2025 Nobel Prize in science with the work honoured:
Prize:
A. Physics
B. Physiology or Medicine
C. Chemistry
D. Economic Sciences
Work:
1. Innovation-driven economic growth
2. Development of metal–organic frameworks
3. Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in an electric circuit
4. Peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Physics) → 3 (Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in an electric circuit); B (Physiology or Medicine) → 4 (Peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells); C (Chemistry) → 2 (Development of metal–organic frameworks); D (Economic Sciences) → 1 (Innovation-driven economic growth).
Physics: Clarke, Devoret, Martinis; Medicine: Brunkow, Ramsdell, Sakaguchi.

questions.q:
In October 2025 the EPFO's Central Board of Trustees approved changes to partial withdrawals. Consider the following:
1. Thirteen separate withdrawal provisions were merged into three broad categories.
2. Members must keep a minimum part of their contribution in the account at all times.
3. Partial withdrawal was abolished for housing purposes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The categories cover essential needs (illness, education, marriage), housing needs and special circumstances; 25% of contributions must remain as a minimum balance.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The UN declared 2025 the International Year of Glaciers' Preservation.
Reason (R): Glaciers store a large share of the world's freshwater and are retreating as the climate warms.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains the reason for the designation.

questions.q:
Consider the following infrastructure projects opened in 2025:
1. The Chenab Rail Bridge, the world's highest railway arch bridge.
2. The new Pamban vertical-lift railway sea bridge.
3. Navi Mumbai International Airport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three were opened in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Operation Sindoor (May 2025):
1. It followed the terrorist attack at Pahalgam in April 2025.
2. It targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
3. It was a joint operation with the United States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It was an Indian operation.

questions.q:
Consider the following about PM-POSHAN:
1. It provides hot cooked meals in government and government-aided schools.
2. It covers children from Balvatika to Class VIII.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is implemented by the Ministry of Education.

questions.q:
Which of the following bodies are chaired by the Prime Minister?
1. NITI Aayog
2. National Development Council (historically)
3. Inter-State Council
4. GST Council
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024:
1. It relates to simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
2. It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
3. It also mandates simultaneous elections to municipalities and panchayats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Local bodies were left to a separate process recommended by the Kovind committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following about inter-State river water disputes:
1. Article 262 lets Parliament provide by law for their adjudication.
2. Parliament may exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over such disputes.
3. A tribunal's award binds the parties only after the President gives assent to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Once published, an award has the same force as a Supreme Court order; there is no Presidential assent.

questions.q: The President returns a Bill (not a Money Bill) to Parliament for reconsideration, and Parliament passes it again without amendment. The President:
o: May refer it to the Supreme Court and withhold assent
questions.x: Correct answer: Must give assent. Article 111: assent cannot be withheld when the Bill is re-passed.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The 73rd Amendment requires a State Finance Commission every five years.
Reason (R): Panchayats depend on devolution of funds from the State, which needs periodic review.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Governor:
1. The Governor may reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President.
2. The Governor can promulgate ordinances when the State legislature is not in session.
3. The Governor can be removed by impeachment by the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President; there is no impeachment procedure for Governors.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Fifth and Sixth Schedules:
1. The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
2. Autonomous District Councils exist under the Sixth Schedule.
3. Tribes Advisory Councils are a feature of the Fifth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes India's 'secularism' as interpreted by courts?
o: Equal respect and treatment of all religions by the State, with the State free to regulate secular aspects
Complete separation with no State engagement with religion
State patronage of a majority religion
questions.x: Correct answer: Equal respect and treatment of all religions by the State, with the State free to regulate secular aspects. S. R. Bommai treated secularism as part of the basic structure.

questions.q: Which of the following is protected by Article 20?
o: Protection against double jeopardy, ex post facto criminal laws and self-incrimination
questions.x: Correct answer: Protection against double jeopardy, ex post facto criminal laws and self-incrimination. Article 22 deals with arrest and preventive detention.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Department-related Standing Committees:
1. They examine Demands for Grants of ministries.
2. Each has members from both Houses.
3. They can examine Bills referred to them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; there are 24 such committees.

questions.q:
Match the case with the principle it is best known for:
Case:
A. Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
B. Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
C. Minerva Mills (1980)
D. S. R. Bommai (1994)
Principle:
1. Limits on the use of Article 356
2. Basic structure doctrine
3. Free and fair elections as part of the basic structure
4. Balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Kesavananda Bharati (1973)) → 2 (Basic structure doctrine); B (Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)) → 3 (Free and fair elections as part of the basic structure); C (Minerva Mills (1980)) → 4 (Balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles); D (S. R. Bommai (1994)) → 1 (Limits on the use of Article 356).
Landmark Constitution Bench decisions.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 44th Amendment (1978):
1. It replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352.
2. It allowed the President to return the advice of the Council of Ministers once for reconsideration.
3. It made the right to property a Fundamental Right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It removed property from the Fundamental Rights.

questions.q:
Match the institution with its primary role:
Institution:
A. NABARD
B. SIDBI
C. IRDAI
D. PFRDA
Role:
1. Regulation of NPS and APY
2. Refinance and development of rural credit
3. Regulation of insurance
4. Finance and development of MSMEs
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (NABARD) → 2 (Refinance and development of rural credit); B (SIDBI) → 4 (Finance and development of MSMEs); C (IRDAI) → 3 (Regulation of insurance); D (PFRDA) → 1 (Regulation of NPS and APY).
Sectoral regulators and development banks.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 20% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹700 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.2 = 5.
Total deposits = 700 × 5 = ₹3,500 crore (of which new credit = ₹2,800 crore).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Economic Survey 2024–25:
1. It is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs.
2. It is presented in Parliament before the Union Budget.
3. It is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Survey is prepared under the Chief Economic Adviser.

questions.q:
When prices are rising, consider the following:
1. FIFO gives a higher closing inventory than the weighted average method.
2. FIFO shows a higher profit than the weighted average method.
3. LIFO is permitted under Ind AS 2.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ind AS 2 does not allow LIFO.

questions.q: Expenditure of ₹2,000 on a calculator, expected to last five years, is charged to the P&L account in the year of purchase. The convention applied is:
questions.x: Small amounts may be expensed even if they benefit more than one period.

questions.q: Office furniture is purchased for ₹3,70,000 and ₹7,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 10 years with a residual value of ₹10,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (3,70,000 + 7,000 − 10,000) / 10 = 3,67,000 / 10 = ₹36,700 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹30,000, closing inventory is ₹20,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹1,25,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (30,000 + 20,000) / 2 = ₹25,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 1,25,000 / 25,000 = 5 times.

questions.q: Interest on drawings of ₹1,200 is charged to the proprietor. The entry is:
o: Cash A/c Dr. To Interest A/c
Interest A/c Dr. To Drawings A/c
Drawings (or Capital) A/c Dr. To Interest on Drawings A/c
Interest on Drawings A/c Dr. To Capital A/c
questions.x: Correct answer: Drawings (or Capital) A/c Dr. To Interest on Drawings A/c. It is an income of the business and reduces the owner's capital.

questions.q: Stock worth ₹2,00,000 is insured for ₹1,50,000 under a policy with an average clause. A fire causes a loss of ₹80,000. The claim admissible is:
Profits of a firm for the last three years were ₹60,000, ₹80,000 and ₹1,00,000. Goodwill is to be valued at two years' purchase of average profits. What is the goodwill?
Annual demand is 4,800 units, ordering cost ₹150 per order and carrying cost ₹4 per unit per year. The economic order quantity is:

Consider the following types of audit:
1. Statutory audit is compulsory under law.
2. Internal audit is mandatory for every company regardless of size.
3. Cost audit relates to verification of cost records maintained under law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Internal audit is mandatory only for prescribed classes of companies.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹4,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 10% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 4,000 = ₹48,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 48,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹2,400.

questions.q: A club received subscriptions of ₹60,000 during 2025–26, which include ₹4,000 for 2024–25 and ₹6,000 for 2026–27. Subscriptions of ₹3,000 for 2025–26 are outstanding. Income from subscriptions for 2025–26 is:
questions.x: 60,000 − 4,000 (previous year) − 6,000 (advance) + 3,000 (outstanding) = ₹53,000.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,05,000; selling price ₹105 and variable cost ₹75 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹60,000?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (1,05,000 + 60,000) / 30 = 5,500 units.

questions.q: An employer argues that its in-house canteen, run by a contractor, is outside its control. Which line of reasoning would courts typically apply to test whether canteen workers are its employees?
o: Whether the canteen is a statutory obligation and the degree of control and integration with the establishment
Only the name on the pay slip
Only whether the contractor is registered
questions.x: Courts examine statutory obligation, control and integration (e.g., Indian Petrochemicals v. Shramik Sena, 1999).

questions.q: Under the IR Code, a settlement reached between the employer and workers outside conciliation (bipartite) binds:
o: All present and future workers of the establishment
Only the parties to the agreement
questions.x: Only conciliation settlements and awards bind all workers; bipartite settlements bind the parties.

questions.q: Which appraisal method sets goals jointly by superior and subordinate and evaluates achievement against them?
questions.x: Correct answer: Management by Objectives. MBO was popularised by Peter Drucker.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes the 'national floor wage' from a State's minimum wage under the Code on Wages?
o: States may set minimum wages below the floor wage for agriculture
The floor wage applies only to central government employees
The floor wage is a lower bound set by the Centre; States set minimum wages at or above it
The floor wage replaces all State minimum wages
questions.x: Section 9: no appropriate government shall fix minimum wages below the floor wage.

questions.q: An adult worker worked 186 days in a factory in 2025. How much annual leave with wages is earned for 2026 under the OSH Code?
o: No leave, as 240 days are required
questions.x: Eligibility is 180 days (240 under the old Factories Act). Leave accrues at one day for every twenty days worked: 186 ÷ 20 = 9.3; a fraction of less than half a day is ignored, so 9 days.

questions.q: A woman employee in a 60-employee firm returns after maternity leave; her child is 10 months old. Which of the following must the employer provide?
o: Paid leave for one more year
Work from home as a right
Access to a creche and two nursing breaks a day
questions.x: Creche (50+ employees) and nursing breaks until 15 months; work from home is by mutual agreement.

questions.q: In Dunlop's systems model, the 'web of rules' is best understood as:
o: The network of trade unions in a country
The procedural and substantive rules produced by the actors to govern the workplace
questions.x: Correct answer: The procedural and substantive rules produced by the actors to govern the workplace. The output of the IR system is a web of rules.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 (now in the Code on Social Security):
1. The employer was not liable if the injury did not disable the worker for more than three days.
2. The employer was not liable if the accident was directly attributable to the worker being under the influence of drink or drugs, unless it resulted in death or permanent total disablement.
3. Compensation was payable for occupational diseases listed in a schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are well-known features: the 3-day waiting period, the exceptions in Section 3, and Schedule III occupational diseases.

questions.q: An Indian IT firm posts an engineer to a country with which India has a Social Security Agreement for 3 years. Which document allows the engineer to keep contributing in India and avoid contributing in the host country?
o: Certificate of Coverage issued by EPFO
questions.x: Correct answer: Certificate of Coverage issued by EPFO. Detachment under an SSA is evidenced by a Certificate of Coverage.

questions.q:
Consider the following duties of an employer under the OSH Code:
1. Ensure the workplace is free from hazards likely to cause injury or occupational disease.
2. Provide free annual health examination to employees of a prescribed age group.
3. Report accidents causing death or serious bodily injury to the authorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are employer duties under the Code.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Voluntary retirement does not amount to retrenchment.
Reason (R): Retrenchment excludes termination by voluntary retirement, superannuation and non-renewal of a fixed-term contract.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The statutory exclusions explain A.

questions.q:
With reference to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (now subsumed in the Code on Wages), consider the following:
1. Wages could be paid in current coin or currency notes, or by cheque/bank credit.
2. No wage period could exceed one month.
3. Wages in a railway, factory or establishment with more than 1,000 persons had to be paid before the expiry of the tenth day after the wage period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three were features of the 1936 Act; the Code on Wages now has a uniform 7-day rule for monthly wages.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918 is significant in Indian labour history.
Reason (R): Gandhi undertook a fast in support of the workers and the dispute was settled through arbitration.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The strike led to the Majoor Mahajan Sangh and an early model of arbitration.

questions.q: A worker's last drawn wages are ₹780 per day and service is 7 years 9 months. The establishment (220 workers) retrenches the worker. Retrenchment compensation plus the Worker Re-skilling Fund credit due to this worker total:
questions.x: 8 years count (9 months > 6). Compensation = 15 × 780 × 8 = ₹93,600; Re-skilling Fund = 15 × 780 = ₹11,700. Total ₹1,05,300.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The IR Code raised the Chapter X threshold for prior permission from 100 to 300 workers.
Reason (R): The Code also allows the appropriate government to raise this threshold further by notification.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true, but R states a separate flexibility rather than explaining the reason for A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the constitutional position of social security:
1. Social security and social insurance are in the Concurrent List.
2. Relief of the disabled and unemployable is in the State List.
3. Old-age pensions and provident funds are exclusively Union subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Provident funds, invalidity and old-age pensions and maternity benefits are in Entry 24 of the Concurrent List.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): EPFO raised the auto-settlement limit for advance claims to ₹5 lakh in 2025.
Reason (R): Auto-settlement processes claims through IT checks without manual intervention, reducing settlement time.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Faster processing is the purpose of auto-settlement.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹26,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 26,000 = ₹3,120.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 3,120 − 1,250 = ₹1,870.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the National Social Assistance Programme:
1. The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme covers BPL persons aged 60 and above.
2. The National Family Benefit Scheme pays a lump sum on the death of the primary breadwinner.
3. NSAP is run under an Act of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
NSAP is a centrally sponsored scheme, not a statutory one.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹820. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹820 × 84 = ₹68,880. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹59,040.)

questions.q: A 30-year-old bank customer joins both PMJJBY and PMSBY. What is the total annual premium payable?
questions.x: PMJJBY ₹436 + PMSBY ₹20 = ₹456 a year.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS):
1. It is available as an option to Central Government employees covered under NPS.
2. It guarantees a minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month after at least ten years of service.
3. Family pension under UPS is 60% of the pension being drawn.
4. It came into effect from 1 April 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct; Statement 4 is correct.
All four are correct.

questions.q: An employee earning ₹35,000 a month suffers permanent total disablement from an employment injury. If the relevant factor is 169.44 and compensation wages are capped at ₹15,000, the compensation is:
questions.x:
Permanent total disablement: 60% of monthly wages × relevant factor (minimum ₹1,40,000).
0.6 × 15,000 × 169.44 = ₹15,24,960 → payable ₹15,24,960.

questions.q:
Consider the following about storage units:
1. One kibibyte (KiB) equals 1,024 bytes.
2. One byte has 8 bits.
3. A nibble has 8 bits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A nibble has 4 bits.

questions.q:
Consider the following about digestion:
1. Salivary amylase begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.
2. Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach.
3. Bile contains enzymes that digest fat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Bile has no enzymes; it emulsifies fats so that lipase can act.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Permafrost thaw can speed up global warming.
Reason (R): Greenhouse gases released by thawing permafrost trap more heat, which causes further thaw.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. This is a positive feedback loop.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Clocks on GPS satellites must be corrected for relativistic effects.
Reason (R): Weaker gravity at orbital height makes satellite clocks run faster, while their orbital speed makes them run slower.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The net effect is about 38 microseconds a day; without correction, position errors would grow by kilometres daily.

questions.q:
Consider the following about language translators:
1. A compiler translates the whole program before it is run.
2. An interpreter translates and executes a program line by line.
3. An assembler translates high-level language into machine code.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
An assembler translates assembly language.

questions.q:
Match the cyber-attack with its description:
Attack:
A. Phishing
B. Ransomware
C. DDoS attack
D. SQL injection
Description:
1. Malware that encrypts files and demands payment
2. Flooding a server with traffic from many sources
3. Malicious input that alters database queries
4. Fake messages that trick users into giving credentials
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Phishing) → 4 (Fake messages that trick users into giving credentials); B (Ransomware) → 1 (Malware that encrypts files and demands payment); C (DDoS attack) → 2 (Flooding a server with traffic from many sources); D (SQL injection) → 3 (Malicious input that alters database queries).
Common attacks and how they work.

questions.q:
Consider the following about genome-edited rice varieties released in India in 2025:
1. They were developed using CRISPR-Cas based genome editing.
2. They include varieties aimed at higher yield and tolerance to salinity.
3. They contain genes inserted from bacteria, like Bt cotton.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
SDN-1 and SDN-2 editing changes the plant's own genes without inserting foreign DNA, unlike transgenic Bt cotton.

questions.q: Why do stars twinkle while planets generally do not?
o: Stars are point sources whose light is bent unevenly by turbulent air; planets appear as small discs that average out the changes
Stars are nearer to the Earth than planets
Stars give out flashes of light, while planets shine steadily
questions.x: Correct answer: Stars are point sources whose light is bent unevenly by turbulent air; planets appear as small discs that average out the changes. Atmospheric refraction affects a point source more noticeably.

questions.q:
Consider the following about solar photovoltaic cells:
1. They convert sunlight directly into electricity.
2. Crystalline silicon is the most widely used material.
3. Their output increases as panel temperature rises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Higher cell temperature lowers efficiency.

questions.q:
Consider the following about drones in India:
1. The Drone Rules, 2021 simplified the approval process for drones.
2. India's airspace is divided into green, yellow and red zones for drone operation.
3. Drones of all sizes need a remote pilot certificate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Nano drones and drones for non-commercial use up to a certain weight are exempt.

questions.q:
Consider the following about rainbows:
1. They are formed by dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops.
2. A rainbow is seen when the Sun is behind the observer.
3. In the primary rainbow, violet appears on the outer edge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Red is on the outer edge of the primary bow.

questions.q:
Consider the following about CRISPR-Cas9:
1. It uses a guide RNA to direct the Cas9 enzyme to a specific DNA sequence.
2. It can be used to cut and edit genes.
3. It was developed from a defence system found in bacteria.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Bacteria use CRISPR to recognise and cut viral DNA.

questions.q: Cells A1 to A5 contain 4, 8, blank, 6 and 'NA' (text). What does =AVERAGE(A1:A5) return?
questions.x: AVERAGE ignores blank and text cells: (4 + 8 + 6) / 3 = 6.

questions.q:
Consider the following about groundwater contaminants in India:
1. Fluoride above about 1.5 mg/L can cause dental and skeletal fluorosis.
2. Arsenic contamination is a major concern in parts of the Ganga–Brahmaputra plains.
3. Nitrate contamination mainly comes from volcanic activity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Nitrate contamination comes mainly from fertilisers and sewage.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2021: 230  |  2022: 205  |  2023: 230  |  2024: 270  |  2025: 275.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2022: -10.87%; 2023: 12.2%; 2024: 17.39%; 2025: 1.85%.
Highest growth: 2024 (17.39%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: An article is marked 60% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 20% and 15% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 160.
After 20%: 128; after a further 15%: 108.8.
Net = 108.8 − 100 = 8.8 → 8.8% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (20% + 15% ≠ 35%).

questions.q: Find the remainder when 5^257 is divided by 13.
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹51.20. The sum is:
At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 5 years. In how many years will it become 4 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 5 years, i.e. rate = 100/5 = 20% p.a.
To become 4 times, interest must be 3 × principal.
Time = (3 × 100) / 20 = 15 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 3, 4, 10, 33, 136, ?

A field officer starts from point O and walks 13 km towards North, then turns left and walks 17 km, then turns left and walks 25 km, and finally turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +13 -25 = -12 km → 12 km South.
East–West: -17 +22 = 5 km → 5 km East.
Distance = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km, towards South-East.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 330, 426, 570 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 426 − 330 = 96, 570 − 426 = 144.
HCF(96, 144) = 48.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of 58^31 + 59^76.
questions.x:
Only last digits matter.
Unit digit of first term (base ending 8, cycle 8,4,2,6; 31 → position 3) = 2.
Unit digit of second term (base ending 9, cycle 9,1,9,1; 76 → position 4) = 1.
2 + 1 → unit digit 3.

questions.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock point in opposite directions (be in a straight line but opposite)?
questions.x:
At 4:00 the minute hand is 20 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To be opposite it must gain 20 + 30 = 50 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 50 × 60/55 = 600/11 minutes = 54 6/11 minutes past 4.

questions.q: A bag has 4 white and 10 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(10,2)/C(14,2) = 45/91.
Required = 1 − 45/91 = 46/91.

questions.q: A vessel holds 90 litres of pure milk. 9 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 90 × (1 − 9/90)² = 90 × (0.9)² = 72.9 litres.
Removing 2 × 9 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: In a row, Imran is 9th from the left and Tanya is 13th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Imran becomes 14th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Imran occupies Tanya's old place, which is 13th from the right and now 14th from the left.
Total = 14 + 13 − 1 = 26.

questions.q: Two candles of the same length are lit at the same time. The first burns out completely in 11 hours and the second in 2 hours, each burning at a uniform rate. After how long will the first candle be exactly twice as long as the second?
questions.x:
After t hours the first candle has (1 − t/11) of its length left and the second (1 − t/2).
1 − t/11 = 2(1 − t/2) ⇒ t(2/2 − 1/11) = 1 ⇒ t = 11×2/(2×11 − 2) = 22/20 h = 1 h 6 min.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a cistern in 8 hours and 36 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 24 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(8, 36, 24) = 72 units.
Rates: +9, +2, −3 units/hour → net 8 units/hour.
Time = 72 / 8 = 9 hours.
